method: Whole text reads of three stored files, SHA256 and Git blob bytes verified against stored tree. Static analysis only.
findings: rm_hasher_main initializes path_index only when print_in_order is true. The ignore-order callback reads read_succesful[session->path_index], rather than read_succesful[index], so that branch uses an uninitialized index. Static defect, no runtime reproduction yet.

Ordered callback uses NULL digest as not-ready marker, but invalid-path dummy callbacks carry NULL and do not advance path_index. A failed position can therefore prevent subsequent completed digests from printing.
Invalid-path handling frees and replaces an interior tag.paths[i] with NULL. Later for-loop condition and g_strfreev use NULL termination, so processing/cleanup of subsequent entries can end early.
stdin path transport splits on newline and cannot represent filenames containing newline. Fixed PATH_MAX line buffer does not detect split long records. No claim about all platform path limits.

Seven test_dedupe.py functions cover equal/different files, hardlinks, arguments, directories, physical reflink transition and shell clone selection. Module-level reflink capability check can skip all; no hash utility failure/order controls are present in this file.
adoption: Retain explicit per-input outcome/index and literal-path transport in own library; no upstream code copied or production optimization claimed.
limits: Only3 files credited in this increment; remaining repository files require review.
No original rmlint build/tests or independent runtime reproduction performed.
Native pHash memory investigation remains deferred; library all-cases goal incomplete.
